dedupe_keys.name: energy service generics and the open energy services community fzi

description: Energy Service Generics is a software framework for turning existing forecasting or optimisation code into fully functional web services, developed to make energy management systems economically viable for buildings and cities by offering forecasting and optimisation as a service. The accompanying paper documents a systematic development from a requirement analysis to a design concept and implementation, and introduces the Open Energy Services community, which maintains the framework and aims to provide ready-to-use forecasting and optimisation services. Coverage: generic; intended for building and city energy management. Access: Python source on GitHub with client and model modules. Licence: Apache 2.0. Caveats: a framework, not a finished service, so forecasting quality depends on the models wrapped, and the community catalogue of services is still growing. Simulation uses: deploying load and PV forecasts or optimisation routines that energy management systems and building digital twins can call. Related records: the Google Smart Buildings dataset and SbSim, and the OpenStudio Server analysis framework.
